===== graphhelm --help
GraphHelm Foundation Graph Kernel

Usage: graphhelm [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  graph        
  schema       
  extension    Extension package operations. Validation stays offline; the lifecycle subcommands (install, switch, rollback, uninstall) act on an install root under an exclusive claim
  development  Development-contract Runtime services (#223), exposed identically here, over MCP, and over HTTP. This surface is under construction: the existence-parity guard in `apps/cli/tests/development_surface_parity.rs` is what keeps the three adapters honest about which operation families actually exist as it grows
  events       
  tasks        Record the end of a lane's external agent process
  execution    
  gateway      
  tool         Invokes one brokered tool call against a project (Tier 0 reads in place, Tier 1 in an ephemeral worktree), producing a digest-only record and operator-side captured streams
  serve        
  mcp          Serves the chat surface: a stateless MCP server over stdio whose tools map 1:1 onto Public Runtime API requests. Speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 until stdin closes
  wake-wait    The wake doorbell's sidecar: creates the rendezvous for an opaque id, blocks for free, exits 0 on ring / 3 on timeout / 2 on unusable arguments. Content never crosses: the woken host learns only THAT it should re-read its log
  quality      Quality-gate operations: the thymus ritual and the certification stamp
  init         First run in a project (#1062): provisions `<project>/.graphhelm/` — the events directory, the bearer token `serve` will read, the sealing key and keyring the Studio's message box needs — registers the MCP server with the chat harnesses it detects, ignores the directory in git, and prints the exact next commands. Idempotent: an existing token or key is kept, never rotated. Neither secret is ever printed
  setup        Read-only inventory and preview for adopting GraphHelm methodology into supported hosts
  backup       Creates a local, verified checkpoint of supported host configuration files
  restore      Preview or apply an exact reviewed, offline configuration restore
  keel         Build, verify, or query the Keel contract index, or check a diff against its card
  journeys     The proven-journey map of the project (#315, #332): each contract step with its newest screen capture from any run, marked fresh, stale or unknown against the project's git history, and the walked arrows between steps. Read-only; identical to `GET /v1/journeys` (and to `GET /v1/executions/{id}/journeys` when `--execution` is given)
  journey      Record journey proof into a run (#315): `capture` one screen of a contract step at the project's current git revision, or `walked` one transition between two captured, consecutive steps
  workspace    Agent workspaces (#360): `claim` a worktree with its own cargo target, temp and log directories under one root, `release` it when the task is done, `list` them, and `sweep` (the owner's) removes released workspaces that are still clean at the released commit
  studio       The Studio: `graphhelm studio start` brings the GraphHelm clone up to date and opens the Studio for the project in the current directory, starting its Runtime when none answers
  update       Update GraphHelm itself: fast-forward the clone this binary comes from to `origin/main` (only a clean `main`), then reinstall the CLI from it with `cargo install`
  skills       Install and keep current the bundled GraphHelm skills in a host's own skills directory
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

  -V, --version
          Print version

===== graphhelm development --help
Development-contract Runtime services (#223), exposed identically here, over MCP, and over HTTP. This surface is under construction: the existence-parity guard in `apps/cli/tests/development_surface_parity.rs` is what keeps the three adapters honest about which operation families actually exist as it grows

Usage: graphhelm development [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  resolve-contract  Resolve layered code rules into one contract (#218's resolver, exposed here)
  memory-status     Report the governed memory states, transitions, and the moves policy allows (#220)
  present           Render an owner-facing presentation from a task result (#219's renderer, exposed here)
  compile-context   Compile a context capsule (#222/#273's compiler, exposed here)
  memory-propose    Propose caller-supplied content for governed memory and report the admission verdict
  dream-shadow      Run one explicit deterministic Dreams shadow and record its advisory result (#72)
  accounting        Report a context-accounting receipt (#222/#273's accounting types, exposed here)
  help              Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm development compile-context --help
Compile a context capsule (#222/#273's compiler, exposed here)

Usage: graphhelm development compile-context [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --budget <BUDGET>
          Token budget the compiled capsule must fit within.
          
          Defaults to zero so the argument-free invocation keeps its existing meaning: with no required sections the required budget is zero, which fits any budget, so the degenerate capsule still compiles and the existence-parity guard still passes.
          
          [default: 0]

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --require <REQUIRE>
          A required context section. Repeatable.
          
          Required context is never dropped to fit: if it does not fit, the command refuses. Trimming it would return a capsule, under budget, missing evidence the caller was required to see.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm development dream-shadow --help
Run one explicit deterministic Dreams shadow and record its advisory result (#72)

Usage: graphhelm development dream-shadow [OPTIONS] --input <INPUT>

Options:
      --input <INPUT>
          Bounded JSON input describing the shadow snapshot

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --trigger <TRIGGER>
          [default: manual]

      --category <CATEGORY>
          [default: code_finding]

      --run-id <RUN_ID>
          [default: dream-run]

      --planner-id <PLANNER_ID>
          [default: dream-planner]

      --critic-id <CRITIC_ID>
          [default: independent-critic]

      --reject
          Refuse the proposal at the independent critic step

      --events <EVENTS>
          Optional local event-store directory for the append-only result

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm events --help
Usage: graphhelm events [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  verify   Verifies a repository's format and, when a range is supplied, its hash chain
  rebuild  Rebuilds a disposable projection generation from retained canonical history
  backup   Writes a new backup archive. An existing target is never overwritten
  restore  Restores an archive into an empty target
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm events backup --help
Writes a new backup archive. An existing target is never overwritten.

`--repository` backs up a local filesystem store; `--config` backs up the configured Postgres database. They are mutually exclusive.

Usage: graphhelm events backup [OPTIONS] --output <OUTPUT>

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --repository <REPOSITORY>
          

      --config <CONFIG>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --output <OUTPUT>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm events restore --help
Restores an archive into an empty target.

With `--config`, the destination is the database named by the configuration's `adminUrl`, which is why no target flag is taken in that mode: the operator refuses to proceed unless that database is fresh. With `--repository`, the destination IS that path — a local store has no configuration naming it, so the flag that selects the mode also names the target.

Usage: graphhelm events restore [OPTIONS] --archive <ARCHIVE>

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --repository <REPOSITORY>
          

      --config <CONFIG>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --archive <ARCHIVE>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm execution --help
Usage: graphhelm execution [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  start          Publishes a graph, starts an execution and drives it to quiescence
  list           Lists the execution streams the event store holds: one summary row per stream, ordered by execution id, sliced by `--after` (exclusive) and `--limit`
  status         Replays a stream and reports the execution's current state — the operator's triage view
  briefing       Replays a stream and reports the resume briefing: what the execution is for, every decision with its actor in order, the work done, what is pending, and the next step. Derived from the store alone; the first thing to read when picking up a run another session or harness drove
  signal         Admits a Graph Signal envelope and reports the governance verdict for the mode in force
  delivery       Record what a node delivered and why, with project-relative file and journey references. Claims are agent-reported; this command does not verify filesystem changes
  document-read  Read a delivery's referenced text document from the explicitly selected main project
  document-save  Save an owner edit to the main project and record the change notice
  approve        The owner approves a `Ghost` or `Blocked` node, readying it. Does not auto-drive: nothing auto-starts out of a manual intervention (D-020); run `resume` to continue
  assign         Assigns an approved ghost node to an agent by its authenticated actor id
  amend-budget   Declares how long one node may stay silent before it needs you, valid from now forward. Use it when `execution status` answers `unknown` for a node: the answer names this command as its remedy
  pause          Holds every edge-eligible node, refusing unless the aggregate status is unset or `Running`
  resume         Recovers any crashed node, gates on the resume preconditions, then re-dispatches exactly the nodes the pause held and drives to quiescence again. `--file` names the graph the execution started with — the driver has no other source of the spec to drive against
  sweep          Evaluates the stream's customs stages and journals the result: one `sweep_performed`, plus one `overdue_exception` for every episode found lapsed, appended together
  claim          Claim that a `waiting_input` node's external work is done, presenting evidence. Testimony only: nothing is released until `execution clear` countersigns. A claim the pipeline cannot accept is journaled as `completion_refused` with its registry code
  clear          Countersign a claim by machine replay: present the digest of the evidence bundle you hold. A matching digest clears the node and drives its dependents; a mismatch is journaled as a rejection and drives nothing
  cancel         Cancels every non-terminal node and completes the execution as `Cancelled`. Refuses when the execution is already terminal
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm execution amend-budget --help
Declares how long one node may stay silent before it needs you, valid from now forward. Use it when `execution status` answers `unknown` for a node: the answer names this command as its remedy.

Earlier versions of this text explained the finding that produced the command instead of what the command does. A newcomer probe read it and concluded the project had an audience of two people, which was fair.

Answers with the RECOMPUTED verdict, never a bare ok -- a write that says "done" forces a second read, and between them two surfaces can disagree about whether the operator may sleep.

Usage: graphhelm execution amend-budget [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS> --node <NODE> --seconds <SECONDS> --at <AT>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --node <NODE>
          

      --seconds <SECONDS>
          The bound the OPERATOR decides. Nothing suggests a value: a default here would turn "absent means unknown" into "absent means 300s" through the back door

      --at <AT>
          The frontier this was computed against, from the verdict that asked for it. An amendment the store cannot place is refused, never guessed

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm execution approve --help
The owner approves a `Ghost` or `Blocked` node, readying it. Does not auto-drive: nothing auto-starts out of a manual intervention (D-020); run `resume` to continue

Usage: graphhelm execution approve [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS> --node <NODE>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --node <NODE>
          

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          Sealed keyring used to recover the exact proposal and authoring snapshot

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          Key id inside `keyring`

      --actor-id <ACTOR_ID>
          Agent actor id to assign after the owner approval is committed

      --proposal-digest <PROPOSAL_DIGEST>
          Full sha256 digest of the sealed proposal under review

      --draft-id <DRAFT_ID>
          Exact sealed draft identifier reviewed by the owner

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm execution claim --help
Claim that a `waiting_input` node's external work is done, presenting evidence. Testimony only: nothing is released until `execution clear` countersigns. A claim the pipeline cannot accept is journaled as `completion_refused` with its registry code

Usage: graphhelm execution claim [OPTIONS] --file <FILE> --events <EVENTS> --node <NODE> --evidence <EVIDENCE>

Options:
      --file <FILE>
          The graph this execution started from — checked against the recorded hash, and the source of the node's declared `completion.customs.proofKinds`

      --pretty
          

      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --node <NODE>
          

      --wait-seq <WAIT_SEQ>
          The envelope sequence of the exact open wait this answers. Absent: the node's open wait

      --evidence <EVIDENCE>
          A JSON array of `{"kind","contentHash","size"}` — the wire shape of `ClaimEvidence`

      --asserter <ASSERTER>
          Who asserts the completion. Absent: the owner actor this command runs as

      --mode <MODE>
          `operator_attested` (default) or `machine_verified`
          
          [default: operator_attested]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm execution clear --help
Countersign a claim by machine replay: present the digest of the evidence bundle you hold. A matching digest clears the node and drives its dependents; a mismatch is journaled as a rejection and drives nothing

Usage: graphhelm execution clear [OPTIONS] --file <FILE> --events <EVENTS> --claim-seq <CLAIM_SEQ>

Options:
      --file <FILE>
          

      --pretty
          

      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --fixtures <FIXTURES>
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --claim-seq <CLAIM_SEQ>
          

      --manifest-hash <MANIFEST_HASH>
          `sha256:<64 hex>` — the bundle digest computed elsewhere. Exactly one of this and `--evidence`

      --evidence <EVIDENCE>
          The bundle itself (same JSON shape as `claim --evidence`); its digest is computed here

      --verifier <VERIFIER>
          Only `machine_replay` exists today; `countersign` is refused and names the decision that will supply it
          
          [default: machine_replay]

  -h, --help
          Print help

      --delivery <DELIVERY>
          

      --project-directory <PROJECT>
          Main project filesystem directory; execution stream scope remains fixed

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

      --actor-id <ACTOR_ID>
          Record the calling agent's identity. Omit for an owner-entered report

  -h, --help
          Print help

Usage: graphhelm execution help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  start          Publishes a graph, starts an execution and drives it to quiescence
  list           Lists the execution streams the event store holds: one summary row per stream, ordered by execution id, sliced by `--after` (exclusive) and `--limit`
  status         Replays a stream and reports the execution's current state — the operator's triage view
  briefing       Replays a stream and reports the resume briefing: what the execution is for, every decision with its actor in order, the work done, what is pending, and the next step. Derived from the store alone; the first thing to read when picking up a run another session or harness drove
  signal         Admits a Graph Signal envelope and reports the governance verdict for the mode in force
  delivery       Record what a node delivered and why, with project-relative file and journey references. Claims are agent-reported; this command does not verify filesystem changes
  document-read  Read a delivery's referenced text document from the explicitly selected main project
  document-save  Save an owner edit to the main project and record the change notice
  approve        The owner approves a `Ghost` or `Blocked` node, readying it. Does not auto-drive: nothing auto-starts out of a manual intervention (D-020); run `resume` to continue
  assign         Assigns an approved ghost node to an agent by its authenticated actor id
  amend-budget   Declares how long one node may stay silent before it needs you, valid from now forward. Use it when `execution status` answers `unknown` for a node: the answer names this command as its remedy
  pause          Holds every edge-eligible node, refusing unless the aggregate status is unset or `Running`
  resume         Recovers any crashed node, gates on the resume preconditions, then re-dispatches exactly the nodes the pause held and drives to quiescence again. `--file` names the graph the execution started with — the driver has no other source of the spec to drive against
  sweep          Evaluates the stream's customs stages and journals the result: one `sweep_performed`, plus one `overdue_exception` for every episode found lapsed, appended together
  claim          Claim that a `waiting_input` node's external work is done, presenting evidence. Testimony only: nothing is released until `execution clear` countersigns. A claim the pipeline cannot accept is journaled as `completion_refused` with its registry code
  clear          Countersign a claim by machine replay: present the digest of the evidence bundle you hold. A matching digest clears the node and drives its dependents; a mismatch is journaled as a rejection and drives nothing
  cancel         Cancels every non-terminal node and completes the execution as `Cancelled`. Refuses when the execution is already terminal
  help           Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

===== graphhelm execution help amend-budget --help
Declares how long one node may stay silent before it needs you, valid from now forward. Use it when `execution status` answers `unknown` for a node: the answer names this command as its remedy

Usage: graphhelm execution help amend-budget

===== graphhelm execution list --help
Lists the execution streams the event store holds: one summary row per stream, ordered by execution id, sliced by `--after` (exclusive) and `--limit`.

The same answer `GET /v1/executions` replies with. It exists so a client never has to scrape the human monitor page to discover which executions are present.

Usage: graphhelm execution list [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --after <AFTER>
          Exclusive cursor: the last execution id the caller already read

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --limit <LIMIT>
          Page size, 1..=100. Defaults to 20. A larger value is refused, never clamped

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm execution pause --help
Holds every edge-eligible node, refusing unless the aggregate status is unset or `Running`.

`--file` supplies the graph this execution started from. With it, the hold is the driver's edge-eligible set, upstream of capacity planning. Without it, pause falls back to bare state and reports `heldNodesGated: false` rather than making an edge claim. The flag is optional because the graph is not stored on the CLI's own execution streams.

Usage: graphhelm execution pause [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS>

Options:
      --file <FILE>
          

      --pretty
          

      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

Options:

          Print help

===== graphhelm execution signal --help
Admits a Graph Signal envelope and reports the governance verdict for the mode in force.

Its evidence is written to a file YOU name (`--evidence-out`), not to the encrypted evidence store: a signal envelope has none of the content slots that pipeline seals. Encrypted externalization for signals is still unbuilt.

Usage: graphhelm execution signal [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS> --signal <SIGNAL> --evidence-out <EVIDENCE_OUT>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --signal <SIGNAL>
          

      --evidence-out <EVIDENCE_OUT>
          

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          REQUIRED, with `--key-id`. Sealed keyring directory; the 32-byte key arrives out of band via `GRAPHHELM_EVENTS_KEY`.
          
          Have no keyring? Create an empty directory, then run `gateway keyring init --keyring <dir> --key-id <id>` with `GRAPHHELM_EVENTS_KEY` set — that command does not create the directory. Then pass both here.

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          REQUIRED, with `--keyring`. The key id inside that keyring

      --attach <ATTACH>
          A PNG, JPEG or WebP image (at most 8 MiB) sealed as Confidential evidence with the signal. Repeatable, up to 4; the type is read from the file's bytes

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm execution start --help
Publishes a graph, starts an execution and drives it to quiescence

Usage: graphhelm execution start [OPTIONS] --file <FILE> --events <EVENTS> --mode <MODE>

Options:
      --file <FILE>
          

      --pretty
          

      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --fixtures <FIXTURES>
          

      --mode <MODE>
          `autopilot`, `supervised`, or `manual` — D-022's three levels of GRAPH-MUTATION autonomy, and nothing else. `autopilot` lets the Governor accept its own proposed mutations; `supervised` holds a proposal until the owner approves it — something is WAITING for you; `manual` rejects every proposal outright — nothing is queued, nothing waits, the owner changes the graph by other means. It does NOT hold dispatch: a `Ready` node runs identically in every mode (`core/runtime/src/driver.rs` never reads this value) — to hold dispatch, use `execution pause`, not a stricter mode. (#89: this flag previously had no help text at all, and D-022's own "Manual Graph" wording — the qualifier that carries this scope — is absent from every other operator-visible surface too.)

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --held
          Publish the graph and record `execution_started` WITHOUT entering the drive loop, so every node stays `Draft` until an explicit `execution resume` (#90).
          
          `resume` WORKS on the result, which is the half that makes this sentence a promise rather than a description: the hold is recorded as `ExecutionPaused`, because `resume_preconditions` gates on `simulation_status == Paused` and would otherwise answer `NotPaused` to every held execution.
          
          WHERE `Draft` LIVES, since the reply does not show it: `node_states` holds only nodes that have ALREADY changed state, so a node still to be dispatched is ABSENT, and the driver reads that absence as `Draft` (`.get(node).copied().unwrap_or(NodeState::Draft)` -- core/execution/src/attention.rs). A held execution therefore reports `nodeStateCounts.draft` as 0 with both nodes staged. That is the projection's documented encoding for every execution before its first dispatch, not something this flag introduces.
          
          This is the axis `mode` is NOT: `mode` governs graph-MUTATION autonomy and the driver never reads it, so before this flag the only way to stage work without running it was to start (which dispatches) and then pause -- a reaction racing the driver rather than a precondition. Holding dispatch and holding mutation stay orthogonal, which is the reasoning #79 was closed on.

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          Sealing keyring for a governed genesis snapshot

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm execution status --help
Replays a stream and reports the execution's current state — the operator's triage view

Usage: graphhelm execution status [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --html <HTML>
          Also writes the monitor page as a frozen, self-contained HTML snapshot (no refresh tag) to this path — the incident artifact and the live page are the same renderer. The JSON envelope still prints to stdout

      --file <FILE>
          #134: the execution's ACTIVE graph -- the latest version published on its stream, or the graph it started from when nothing was published (the CLI's own streams). With it, the reply carries `dispatch` (`ready` to dispatch, `gated` behind unmet predecessors, `gatedNodes`) derived from the same predicate the driver uses; without it `dispatch` is null and `dispatchUnavailable` says why. Any other graph, the start graph included once a newer one was published, is refused

      --tasks
          #1149: also fold the execution's `task.*` records into `tasks`, the same projection `GET /v1/executions/{id}/tasks` and the MCP tool `tasks` serve. Needs `--execution` and the sealing keyring (`--keyring`, `--key-id`) that opens the envelopes

      --full-tasks
          #1449: with `--tasks`, the whole fold (every record, slice and route of the run's history) instead of the open board `--tasks` answers by default

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm execution sweep --help
Evaluates the stream's customs stages and journals the result: one `sweep_performed`, plus one `overdue_exception` for every episode found lapsed, appended together.

A sweep that finds nothing STILL writes its record. Without it, "no exceptions" and "no sweep ever ran" are the same absence in the log.

`--as-of` asks about a past instant and defaults to now. THE FUTURE IS REFUSED: a future-dated answer is indistinguishable from a real one in the journal, while permanently spending the episodes it touches -- the honest sweep arriving later would find nothing left to raise.

Usage: graphhelm execution sweep [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --as-of <AS_OF>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm extension --help
Extension package operations. Validation stays offline; the lifecycle subcommands (install, switch, rollback, uninstall) act on an install root under an exclusive claim

Usage: graphhelm extension [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  validate          Validates extension.json and every declared contribution in a local package directory
  mint-mcp-token    #213: mints one per-contribution MCP capability token, allowed_tools frozen from the named contribution's own declared `surfaces` at this instant. Prints the token as JSON to stdout (the caller redirects to a file); this command never writes one itself
  install           #212: stage, verify and adopt a package under the install root's versions/ tree. Does not switch; the adopted digest is printed for the switch that follows
  switch            #212: atomically make an adopted version the active one. The target is re-verified at the moment of use, and any refusal leaves the previous version active
  rollback          #212: atomically return to the previous known-good version
  uninstall         #212: remove one adopted version that the active pointer no longer names
  revoke-mcp-token  #213: flips `revoked` on a presented token file's JSON and prints the result to stdout -- every other bound field is untouched. The caller decides where the revoked bytes land (overwrite in place, or a new file); this command never writes one itself
  help              Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm gateway --help
Usage: graphhelm gateway [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  routes      Validates a route manifest and reports every route it declares
  probe       Quota-free health probe (§18) for one route: a `direct_api` route proves its credential leases from the broker; a `native_runtime` route proves its CLI spawns and exits cleanly on `--version`. Never places a real model call and never prints a credential value
  route       Writes one `direct_api` route into a manifest (#1171): the edit `setup` cannot do, and the CLI half of `PUT /v1/gateway/routes`. Never touches a credential value, and never rewrites a `native_runtime` route
  credential  Manages BYOK credentials held in the broker
  keyring     Manages the sealing keyring itself, independently of any credential
  setup       One command that wires a model provider into a project `init` provisioned (#1139): adds the provider's `direct_api` route to `<project>/.graphhelm/manifest.json`, reads the API key ONCE (hidden prompt on a terminal, one line on a pipe; never an argument), stores it in the Credential Broker under the keyring `init` made, probes the route, and prints the next commands. The key never appears in output, logs, or any file outside the sealed broker
  help        Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

  remove  Revokes a credential. A revoked credential can never be leased again, including after the broker is reopened
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

          Print help

Usage: graphhelm gateway keyring help init

===== graphhelm gateway keyring init --help
Creates the sealing key a Runtime needs to seal evidence, and nothing else.

This key encrypts evidence held on this machine. It is not a model credential, is never sent anywhere, and grants access to nothing outside this keyring.

It exists because until now the ONLY way to put a key in a keyring was `gateway credential set`, which stores a BYOK model credential and reads a secret from stdin. A Runtime that seals a message needs the key and does not need a credential, so an operator who wanted only the message path had to invent an API key to get past the setup.

Usage: graphhelm gateway keyring init [OPTIONS] --keyring <KEYRING> --key-id <KEY_ID>

Options:
      --keyring <KEYRING>
          

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm gateway route set --help
Adds or replaces one `direct_api` route in the manifest. The whole document is validated before anything is written, and the write is a temporary file renamed into place, because `serve` re-reads the manifest on every request that resolves a route

Usage: graphhelm gateway route set [OPTIONS] --manifest <MANIFEST> --id <ID> --provider <PROVIDER> --base-url <BASE_URL> --model <MODEL>

Options:
      --manifest <MANIFEST>
          

      --pretty
          

      --id <ID>
          The route id callers will name (`--route`, `"route"` in a request body). Unique within the manifest: an id already present is refused unless `--replace` is given

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          The WIRE FORMAT the adapter selects on, not the vendor: `anthropic`, `openai` or `typesafe` today. A DeepSeek endpoint is an `openai` route with its own base URL

      --base-url <BASE_URL>
          `https://…`, or `http://` to a loopback address. No trailing slash

      --model <MODEL>
          

      --credential-ref <CREDENTIAL_REF>
          The broker reference holding this route's key. Absent: `secret_<id>`, which cannot collide the way a provider-keyed name does when two vendors share one wire format

      --disabled
          Write the route disabled. A disabled route is listed and refused at dispatch, which is how an operator parks a provider without deleting what it took to configure

      --replace
          Replace an existing route with this id. Without it, an existing id is refused and the manifest is left byte-identical

      --tier <TIERS>
          A delegation tier the route serves (`small`, `standard`, `large`); repeat for several. Absent on a replace: the replaced route's tiers are kept (ADR-041)

      --no-tiers
          Write the route with no tiers, clearing any a replaced route declared

      --context-window-tokens <CONTEXT_WINDOW_TOKENS>
          The provider's documented input context window in tokens (ADR-042), which bounds subagent session reuse on this route. `0` clears it. Absent on a replace: the replaced route's window is kept

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm gateway setup --help
One command that wires a model provider into a project `init` provisioned (#1139): adds the provider's `direct_api` route to `<project>/.graphhelm/manifest.json`, reads the API key ONCE (hidden prompt on a terminal, one line on a pipe; never an argument), stores it in the Credential Broker under the keyring `init` made, probes the route, and prints the next commands. The key never appears in output, logs, or any file outside the sealed broker

Usage: graphhelm gateway setup [OPTIONS] --provider <PROVIDER>

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --provider <PROVIDER>
          Possible values:
          - typesafe:  TypeSafe's System One judge (`https://api.typesafe.ai`, model `jev-latest`, route `judge`)
          - anthropic: Anthropic's Messages API (`https://api.anthropic.com`, route `anthropic`; `--model` required)
          - openai:    OpenAI's API (`https://api.openai.com`, route `openai`; `--model` required)

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --project <PROJECT>
          The project `init` provisioned. Defaults to the current directory; must exist

      --route-id <ROUTE_ID>
          The route id written into the manifest; the provider's default when absent

      --model <MODEL>
          The model the route names. Defaulted for `typesafe` only; the other providers publish no single model this command could pin, so it must be given

      --base-url <BASE_URL>
          The route's `baseUrl` (`https://…`, or `http://` to loopback); the provider's when absent

      --replace
          Replace an existing route with the same id. Without it a second run is refused and the manifest is left untouched

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          The sealing key's id inside the keyring, as given to `init`
          
          [default: studio]

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm graph synthesize --help
Compiles a goal into a graph document through a model (#107): one draft, a bounded repair loop, the same validation chain an authored graph takes, and `completion.customs` stamped on every node that can park. Writes the document to `--out` and never publishes or starts it: the file enters the system through `execution start --file` like any other.

The model is either the recorded door (`--fixture`, keyless) or a gateway route (`--manifest --route`, with `--broker --keyring --key-id` for a `direct_api` route); exactly one of the two. Boxed: the flag set is the widest of the family (#1123 added four), and clap implements `Args` for `Box<T>`, so the enum stays the size of its other variants.

Usage: graphhelm graph synthesize [OPTIONS] --goal <GOAL> --out <OUT>

Options:
      --goal <GOAL>
          

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --out <OUT>
          Where the document is written. Must end in `.json` and must not exist yet

      --mode <MODE>
          `autopilot`, `supervised` or `manual`; the profile's default (`supervised`) when absent

      --max-nodes <MAX_NODES>
          

      --allow-program <ALLOW_PROGRAMS>
          Repeatable; the programs a synthesized shell call may name. There is no default: a draft naming any other program is refused, and the architect never widens the list

      --fixture <FIXTURE>
          A `{"replies": {"<prompt sha256>": "<text>"}}` recording (`core/architect/fixtures`)

      --manifest <MANIFEST>
          

      --route <ROUTE>
          

      --broker <BROKER>
          

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

      --judge-route <JUDGE_ROUTE>
          The judge door over a gateway route: a `direct_api` route whose provider is `typesafe`, named in `--manifest` and leased through `--broker --keyring --key-id` like `--route`. Exclusive with `--judge-fixture`; no judge means today's road

      --judge-fixture <JUDGE_FIXTURE>
          The recorded judge door: a `{"answers": {"<request sha256>": <reply>}}` recording (`core/architect/fixtures/judge`)

      --drafts <DRAFTS>
          How many drafts to ask for and rank, 1..=3; more than one needs a judge

      --library <LIBRARY>
          A directory of graph templates (`<id>.yaml` beside `<id>.template.json`) the judge may choose to reuse or adapt; read only when a judge is named

      --critic <CRITIC>
          `design` puts a design step and a blind critic step in front of the draft, the way the task plan's `critic` says (#467); `none` or absent is the draft alone

      --plan <PLAN>
          The task's plan, as `graphhelm --json keel plan` prints it (#467). Without `--critic`, the plan's own `critic` decides whether the design is graded first; `--critic` wins

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          The run this graph is built for (#561). Without `--critic` and `--plan`, the run's own newest trusted `keel.plan` record decides, read from `--events` with `--keyring --key-id`

      --events <EVENTS>
          The events directory `--execution` lives in

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm graph topology --help
Reports a graph file's shape - entrypoints, nodes, edges - plus the semantic hash that says WHICH graph it is.

The hash is the load-bearing field: an execution's log records the graph's hash and never its topology, so a caller that wants to draw a run's graph compares this hash against the `graphHash` in that run's `execution_started` event before believing the edges belong to it. Nodes carry identity only - no objectives, agents or completion controls.

Usage: graphhelm graph topology [OPTIONS] <FILE>

Arguments:
  <FILE>
          

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm help --help
Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Usage: graphhelm help [COMMAND]

Commands:
  graph        
  schema       
  extension    Extension package operations. Validation stays offline; the lifecycle subcommands (install, switch, rollback, uninstall) act on an install root under an exclusive claim
  development  Development-contract Runtime services (#223), exposed identically here, over MCP, and over HTTP. This surface is under construction: the existence-parity guard in `apps/cli/tests/development_surface_parity.rs` is what keeps the three adapters honest about which operation families actually exist as it grows
  events       
  tasks        Record the end of a lane's external agent process
  execution    
  gateway      
  tool         Invokes one brokered tool call against a project (Tier 0 reads in place, Tier 1 in an ephemeral worktree), producing a digest-only record and operator-side captured streams
  serve        
  mcp          Serves the chat surface: a stateless MCP server over stdio whose tools map 1:1 onto Public Runtime API requests. Speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 until stdin closes
  wake-wait    The wake doorbell's sidecar: creates the rendezvous for an opaque id, blocks for free, exits 0 on ring / 3 on timeout / 2 on unusable arguments. Content never crosses: the woken host learns only THAT it should re-read its log
  quality      Quality-gate operations: the thymus ritual and the certification stamp
  init         First run in a project (#1062): provisions `<project>/.graphhelm/` — the events directory, the bearer token `serve` will read, the sealing key and keyring the Studio's message box needs — registers the MCP server with the chat harnesses it detects, ignores the directory in git, and prints the exact next commands. Idempotent: an existing token or key is kept, never rotated. Neither secret is ever printed
  setup        Read-only inventory and preview for adopting GraphHelm methodology into supported hosts
  backup       Creates a local, verified checkpoint of supported host configuration files
  restore      Preview or apply an exact reviewed, offline configuration restore
  keel         Build, verify, or query the Keel contract index, or check a diff against its card
  journeys     The proven-journey map of the project (#315, #332): each contract step with its newest screen capture from any run, marked fresh, stale or unknown against the project's git history, and the walked arrows between steps. Read-only; identical to `GET /v1/journeys` (and to `GET /v1/executions/{id}/journeys` when `--execution` is given)
  journey      Record journey proof into a run (#315): `capture` one screen of a contract step at the project's current git revision, or `walked` one transition between two captured, consecutive steps
  workspace    Agent workspaces (#360): `claim` a worktree with its own cargo target, temp and log directories under one root, `release` it when the task is done, `list` them, and `sweep` (the owner's) removes released workspaces that are still clean at the released commit
  studio       The Studio: `graphhelm studio start` brings the GraphHelm clone up to date and opens the Studio for the project in the current directory, starting its Runtime when none answers
  update       Update GraphHelm itself: fast-forward the clone this binary comes from to `origin/main` (only a clean `main`), then reinstall the CLI from it with `cargo install`
  skills       Install and keep current the bundled GraphHelm skills in a host's own skills directory
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

===== graphhelm help execution --help
Usage: graphhelm help execution [COMMAND]

Commands:
  start          Publishes a graph, starts an execution and drives it to quiescence
  list           Lists the execution streams the event store holds: one summary row per stream, ordered by execution id, sliced by `--after` (exclusive) and `--limit`
  status         Replays a stream and reports the execution's current state — the operator's triage view
  briefing       Replays a stream and reports the resume briefing: what the execution is for, every decision with its actor in order, the work done, what is pending, and the next step. Derived from the store alone; the first thing to read when picking up a run another session or harness drove
  signal         Admits a Graph Signal envelope and reports the governance verdict for the mode in force
  delivery       Record what a node delivered and why, with project-relative file and journey references. Claims are agent-reported; this command does not verify filesystem changes
  document-read  Read a delivery's referenced text document from the explicitly selected main project
  document-save  Save an owner edit to the main project and record the change notice
  approve        The owner approves a `Ghost` or `Blocked` node, readying it. Does not auto-drive: nothing auto-starts out of a manual intervention (D-020); run `resume` to continue
  assign         Assigns an approved ghost node to an agent by its authenticated actor id
  amend-budget   Declares how long one node may stay silent before it needs you, valid from now forward. Use it when `execution status` answers `unknown` for a node: the answer names this command as its remedy
  pause          Holds every edge-eligible node, refusing unless the aggregate status is unset or `Running`
  resume         Recovers any crashed node, gates on the resume preconditions, then re-dispatches exactly the nodes the pause held and drives to quiescence again. `--file` names the graph the execution started with — the driver has no other source of the spec to drive against
  sweep          Evaluates the stream's customs stages and journals the result: one `sweep_performed`, plus one `overdue_exception` for every episode found lapsed, appended together
  claim          Claim that a `waiting_input` node's external work is done, presenting evidence. Testimony only: nothing is released until `execution clear` countersigns. A claim the pipeline cannot accept is journaled as `completion_refused` with its registry code
  clear          Countersign a claim by machine replay: present the digest of the evidence bundle you hold. A matching digest clears the node and drives its dependents; a mismatch is journaled as a rejection and drives nothing
  cancel         Cancels every non-terminal node and completes the execution as `Cancelled`. Refuses when the execution is already terminal

===== graphhelm help execution amend-budget --help
Declares how long one node may stay silent before it needs you, valid from now forward. Use it when `execution status` answers `unknown` for a node: the answer names this command as its remedy

Usage: graphhelm help execution amend-budget

===== graphhelm help extension --help
Extension package operations. Validation stays offline; the lifecycle subcommands (install, switch, rollback, uninstall) act on an install root under an exclusive claim

Usage: graphhelm help extension [COMMAND]

Commands:
  validate          Validates extension.json and every declared contribution in a local package directory
  mint-mcp-token    #213: mints one per-contribution MCP capability token, allowed_tools frozen from the named contribution's own declared `surfaces` at this instant. Prints the token as JSON to stdout (the caller redirects to a file); this command never writes one itself
  install           #212: stage, verify and adopt a package under the install root's versions/ tree. Does not switch; the adopted digest is printed for the switch that follows
  switch            #212: atomically make an adopted version the active one. The target is re-verified at the moment of use, and any refusal leaves the previous version active
  rollback          #212: atomically return to the previous known-good version
  uninstall         #212: remove one adopted version that the active pointer no longer names
  revoke-mcp-token  #213: flips `revoked` on a presented token file's JSON and prints the result to stdout -- every other bound field is untouched. The caller decides where the revoked bytes land (overwrite in place, or a new file); this command never writes one itself

===== graphhelm help extension install --help
#212: stage, verify and adopt a package under the install root's versions/ tree. Does not switch; the adopted digest is printed for the switch that follows

===== graphhelm help gateway --help
Usage: graphhelm help gateway [COMMAND]

Commands:
  routes      Validates a route manifest and reports every route it declares
  probe       Quota-free health probe (§18) for one route: a `direct_api` route proves its credential leases from the broker; a `native_runtime` route proves its CLI spawns and exits cleanly on `--version`. Never places a real model call and never prints a credential value
  route       Writes one `direct_api` route into a manifest (#1171): the edit `setup` cannot do, and the CLI half of `PUT /v1/gateway/routes`. Never touches a credential value, and never rewrites a `native_runtime` route
  credential  Manages BYOK credentials held in the broker
  keyring     Manages the sealing keyring itself, independently of any credential
  setup       One command that wires a model provider into a project `init` provisioned (#1139): adds the provider's `direct_api` route to `<project>/.graphhelm/manifest.json`, reads the API key ONCE (hidden prompt on a terminal, one line on a pipe; never an argument), stores it in the Credential Broker under the keyring `init` made, probes the route, and prints the next commands. The key never appears in output, logs, or any file outside the sealed broker

===== graphhelm help gateway credential --help
Manages BYOK credentials held in the broker

Usage: graphhelm help gateway credential [COMMAND]

Commands:
  set     Stores a credential. The value is read from stdin — one trimmed line — and is never accepted as an argument
  remove  Revokes a credential. A revoked credential can never be leased again, including after the broker is reopened

===== graphhelm help gateway credential remove --help
Revokes a credential. A revoked credential can never be leased again, including after the broker is reopened

Usage: graphhelm help gateway credential remove

===== graphhelm help gateway credential set --help
Stores a credential. The value is read from stdin — one trimmed line — and is never accepted as an argument

Usage: graphhelm help gateway credential set

===== graphhelm help init --help
First run in a project (#1062): provisions `<project>/.graphhelm/` — the events directory, the bearer token `serve` will read, the sealing key and keyring the Studio's message box needs — registers the MCP server with the chat harnesses it detects, ignores the directory in git, and prints the exact next commands. Idempotent: an existing token or key is kept, never rotated. Neither secret is ever printed

===== graphhelm help journey --help
Record journey proof into a run (#315): `capture` one screen of a contract step at the project's current git revision, or `walked` one transition between two captured, consecutive steps

Usage: graphhelm help journey [COMMAND]

Commands:
  capture      Record a `jpd.screen_captured` signal: one image of one contract step, stamped with the project's HEAD and whether the working tree is dirty
  walked       Record a `jpd.transition_walked` signal citing the newest capture of two consecutive steps
  validate     Check journey contracts before anything records against them (#328): the contract schema, the journey id rule, step, actor, promise and screen consistency, and that every screen `scopePaths` entry exists in the project. Exit 0 clean, 2 findings, 3 input error
  compile      Generate frozen journey contracts from flow sources, or check/format their projection
  approve      Approve a canonical flow at the project's HEAD and write its generated contracts
  reject       Reject a flow with the owner's reason (#1588). Owner only. The record binds the flow's current content: editing the flow clears it
  sign-legacy  Record the owner's signature for approvals made before #534 (lists them with the commit that introduced each; writes only for each `--id`)
  mark-safe    Mark one edge of a DRAFT flow safe to watch although an act on it looks destructive (#518). Owner only. The mark binds the edge's acts: editing them voids it
  label        Set a flow's display labels (#1296): its short `--name` and the `--feature` the Studio groups it under. Labels sit outside the approved digest, so an approved flow stays approved
  flows        List every flow source for review: status, drift, validate findings, whether Approve would be accepted, and its screens, edges and paths
  replay       Replay every approved path with the explicitly installed browser observer, without a model
  open         Open an approved flow live at one step (#398): replays the cached acts of the earlier edges in a visible browser, without a model, reports the step's state, and keeps the browser open for `journey act` / `journey close` until the replay run budget ends
  watch        Play a flow, draft or approved, from its entry to its last screen in a visible browser, paced for a person to follow (about 1.5 s per act), without a model. A look at what the flow does before approving it: never proof, never a capture, never an approval. A draft's act that looks destructive (delete, remove, drop, pay, purchase, transfer, send) is not performed, and the play stops there naming it, unless watch itself started the project's declared fixture (#515)
  act          Send one act to an open live session and report the screen it lands on
  close        Close an open live session and its browser
  sessions     List the project's open live sessions and their current state
  preview      Run a flow, draft or approved, headless along every path and keep, per screen, whether it passed and a masked frame of it (#519). Answers the kept result when it is for this flow and commit; otherwise starts a run in the background and answers `running`. Never proof
  explore      Observe a local app through a selected model route and publish an unapproved draft flow
  report       Write one self-contained HTML page of a journey's kept preview (#1448): each step's real frame, the action into it, what the screen must show with what the run saw, and the overall result. Reads the kept preview; starts no run

===== graphhelm help journey act --help
Send one act to an open live session and report the screen it lands on

===== graphhelm help tool code-index query --help
Query an existing immutable Codebase Memory bundle in one fresh workspace

Usage: graphhelm help tool code-index query

===== graphhelm help tool invoke --help
One authorized tool call, end to end: authorize -> route by tier -> execute -> record

Usage: graphhelm help tool invoke

===== graphhelm help update --help
Update GraphHelm itself: fast-forward the clone this binary comes from to `origin/main` (only a clean `main`), then reinstall the CLI from it with `cargo install`

Usage: graphhelm help update

===== graphhelm help wake-wait --help
The wake doorbell's sidecar: creates the rendezvous for an opaque id, blocks for free, exits 0 on ring / 3 on timeout / 2 on unusable arguments. Content never crosses: the woken host learns only THAT it should re-read its log

Usage: graphhelm help wake-wait

===== graphhelm help workspace --help
Agent workspaces (#360): `claim` a worktree with its own cargo target, temp and log directories under one root, `release` it when the task is done, `list` them, and `sweep` (the owner's) removes released workspaces that are still clean at the released commit

Usage: graphhelm help workspace [COMMAND]

Commands:
  claim    Create `<root>/<lane>/<task>/` with a git worktree (`wt`) and `target`, `tmp` and `logs` directories, record the claim, and print the environment to use
  release  Declare the task done: records the worktree's HEAD. Deletes nothing
  list     Every recorded workspace with its state, size and live git facts. Read-only
  sweep    Remove released workspaces that are clean and still at the released commit, ignored files included. A dry run unless `--apply`. Never touches a path the ledger did not create, never follows a link, and keeps any workspace whose worktree contains one
  remove   Remove one worktree or directory without ever following a link (#1663). A linked git worktree is stopped, unlinked, its uncommitted work saved, unregistered and deleted; any other directory has its links unlinked and is deleted. Use it instead of `rm -rf` or `git worktree remove --force`, which follow junctions. Exit 3 when it could not finish
  slot     Run one command under the root's build slot: one at a time, in arrival order, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and the current worktree's own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<cwd>/target`. A waiter that dies loses its place by itself (its ticket's OS lock is released). The command's exit code is ours

===== graphhelm help workspace claim --help
Create `<root>/<lane>/<task>/` with a git worktree (`wt`) and `target`, `tmp` and `logs` directories, record the claim, and print the environment to use

Usage: graphhelm help workspace claim

===== graphhelm help workspace list --help
Every recorded workspace with its state, size and live git facts. Read-only

Usage: graphhelm help workspace list

===== graphhelm help workspace release --help
Declare the task done: records the worktree's HEAD. Deletes nothing

Usage: graphhelm help workspace release

===== graphhelm help workspace remove --help
Remove one worktree or directory without ever following a link (#1663). A linked git worktree is stopped, unlinked, its uncommitted work saved, unregistered and deleted; any other directory has its links unlinked and is deleted. Use it instead of `rm -rf` or `git worktree remove --force`, which follow junctions. Exit 3 when it could not finish

Usage: graphhelm help workspace remove

===== graphhelm help workspace slot --help
Run one command under the root's build slot: one at a time, in arrival order, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and the current worktree's own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<cwd>/target`. A waiter that dies loses its place by itself (its ticket's OS lock is released). The command's exit code is ours

Usage: graphhelm help workspace slot [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status  Who holds the build slot (lane, label, for how long) and who waits, in order, with their wait. Read-only apart from removing a dead waiter's ticket

===== graphhelm help workspace slot status --help
Who holds the build slot (lane, label, for how long) and who waits, in order, with their wait. Read-only apart from removing a dead waiter's ticket

Usage: graphhelm help workspace slot status

===== graphhelm help workspace sweep --help
Remove released workspaces that are clean and still at the released commit, ignored files included. A dry run unless `--apply`. Never touches a path the ledger did not create, never follows a link, and keeps any workspace whose worktree contains one

Usage: graphhelm help workspace sweep

===== graphhelm init --help
First run in a project (#1062): provisions `<project>/.graphhelm/` — the events directory, the bearer token `serve` will read, the sealing key and keyring the Studio's message box needs — registers the MCP server with the chat harnesses it detects, ignores the directory in git, and prints the exact next commands. Idempotent: an existing token or key is kept, never rotated. Neither secret is ever printed

Usage: graphhelm init [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --project <PROJECT>
          The project directory to provision. Defaults to the current directory; must exist

      --bind <BIND>
          The loopback address the Runtime will bind; written into every harness registration and every printed command, so one number is used everywhere (`install.sh` uses 8080 on a VPS)
          
          [default: 127.0.0.1:8791]

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          The sealing key's id inside the keyring
          
          [default: studio]

      --harness <HARNESS>
          Which chat harnesses to register, repeatable. Absent: every harness detected on this machine (`claude-code` when `.claude/` exists in the project or `~/.claude` exists; `codex` when `~/.codex` exists)

          Possible values:
          - claude-code: Claude Code: `<project>/.mcp.json`, merged into an existing one
          - codex:       Codex: a `[mcp_servers.graphhelm]` snippet at `<project>/.graphhelm/codex.config.toml` for the operator to append to `~/.codex/config.toml`; the home directory is never written

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm journey --help
Record journey proof into a run (#315): `capture` one screen of a contract step at the project's current git revision, or `walked` one transition between two captured, consecutive steps

Usage: graphhelm journey [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  capture      Record a `jpd.screen_captured` signal: one image of one contract step, stamped with the project's HEAD and whether the working tree is dirty
  walked       Record a `jpd.transition_walked` signal citing the newest capture of two consecutive steps
  validate     Check journey contracts before anything records against them (#328): the contract schema, the journey id rule, step, actor, promise and screen consistency, and that every screen `scopePaths` entry exists in the project. Exit 0 clean, 2 findings, 3 input error
  compile      Generate frozen journey contracts from flow sources, or check/format their projection
  approve      Approve a canonical flow at the project's HEAD and write its generated contracts
  reject       Reject a flow with the owner's reason (#1588). Owner only. The record binds the flow's current content: editing the flow clears it
  sign-legacy  Record the owner's signature for approvals made before #534 (lists them with the commit that introduced each; writes only for each `--id`)
  mark-safe    Mark one edge of a DRAFT flow safe to watch although an act on it looks destructive (#518). Owner only. The mark binds the edge's acts: editing them voids it
  label        Set a flow's display labels (#1296): its short `--name` and the `--feature` the Studio groups it under. Labels sit outside the approved digest, so an approved flow stays approved
  flows        List every flow source for review: status, drift, validate findings, whether Approve would be accepted, and its screens, edges and paths
  replay       Replay every approved path with the explicitly installed browser observer, without a model
  open         Open an approved flow live at one step (#398): replays the cached acts of the earlier edges in a visible browser, without a model, reports the step's state, and keeps the browser open for `journey act` / `journey close` until the replay run budget ends
  watch        Play a flow, draft or approved, from its entry to its last screen in a visible browser, paced for a person to follow (about 1.5 s per act), without a model. A look at what the flow does before approving it: never proof, never a capture, never an approval. A draft's act that looks destructive (delete, remove, drop, pay, purchase, transfer, send) is not performed, and the play stops there naming it, unless watch itself started the project's declared fixture (#515)
  act          Send one act to an open live session and report the screen it lands on
  close        Close an open live session and its browser
  sessions     List the project's open live sessions and their current state
  preview      Run a flow, draft or approved, headless along every path and keep, per screen, whether it passed and a masked frame of it (#519). Answers the kept result when it is for this flow and commit; otherwise starts a run in the background and answers `running`. Never proof
  explore      Observe a local app through a selected model route and publish an unapproved draft flow
  report       Write one self-contained HTML page of a journey's kept preview (#1448): each step's real frame, the action into it, what the screen must show with what the run saw, and the overall result. Reads the kept preview; starts no run
  help         Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm journey act --help
Send one act to an open live session and report the screen it lands on

Usage: graphhelm journey act [OPTIONS] --kind <KIND> --role <ROLE> --name <NAME> <SESSION>

Arguments:
  <SESSION>
          The session id `journey open` printed

Options:
      --kind <KIND>
          `activate`, `submit`, `enter_text`, `navigate`, `wait_for` or `inspect`

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --role <ROLE>
          

      --name <NAME>
          The control's exact accessible name

      --text <TEXT>
          Literal text for `enter_text`

      --secret <SECRET>
          A flow secret name for `enter_text`; its value was supplied to `journey open`

      --project <PROJECT>
          

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm journey capture --help
Record a `jpd.screen_captured` signal: one image of one contract step, stamped with the project's HEAD and whether the working tree is dirty

Usage: graphhelm journey capture [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS> --execution <EXECUTION> --keyring <KEYRING> --key-id <KEY_ID> --contract <CONTRACT> --step <STEP> --image <IMAGE>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          The keyring that seals the signal envelope

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

      --project <PROJECT>
          The git project whose `.graphhelm/journeys/` holds the contract. Defaults to the current directory

      --contract <CONTRACT>
          

      --step <STEP>
          

      --image <IMAGE>
          A PNG, JPEG or WebP image of the screen

      --viewport <VIEWPORT>
          `WIDTHxHEIGHT`; required unless the image is a PNG, whose header carries both

      --pr <PR>
          

      --phase <PHASE>
          `before`, `after`, or `live` (a `journey open` session at its step, #398)

  -h, --help
          Print help

Usage: graphhelm journey open [OPTIONS] --step <STEP> <ID>

          The flow id (`<id>.journey.yaml`)

      --pretty
          

      --step <STEP>
          The screen id to open at

      --path <PATH>
          The named path to walk; defaults to the first path that reaches the step (`main` first)

      --project <PROJECT>

      --execution <EXECUTION>

===== graphhelm journey preview --help
Run a flow, draft or approved, headless along every path and keep, per screen, whether it passed and a masked frame of it (#519). Answers the kept result when it is for this flow and commit; otherwise starts a run in the background and answers `running`. Never proof

Usage: graphhelm journey preview [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          The flow id (`<id>.journey.yaml`); a draft is accepted

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --project <PROJECT>
          

      --force
          Run anew even when a current result is kept (the Studio's Run again)

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --read
          Answer the kept result without starting a run

      --confirm
          The owner's click on "Run it?": this run of an approved flow may play its destructive acts (#519). Without it an approved flow stops before the first one. Implies a new run

      --confirm-digest <CONFIRM_DIGEST>
          #1662: with `--confirm` on a draft, the flow digest the owner saw beside its commands. A flow edited since then is refused, so a confirm never allows argv the owner did not see

      --token-file <TOKEN_FILE>
          #1662: the owner's token, required to confirm a draft's commands from the CLI

  -h, --help
          Print help

  <ID>
          The flow id

Options:
      --note <NOTE>
          Why the flow is rejected: what the owner saw (1 to 4096 bytes)

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --project <PROJECT>
          

      --token-file <TOKEN_FILE>
          The project's owner token (`.graphhelm/events.token`): rejecting is the owner's

===== graphhelm journey replay --help
Replay every approved path with the explicitly installed browser observer, without a model

Usage: graphhelm journey replay [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --project <PROJECT>
          

      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

      --allow-origin <ALLOW_ORIGIN>
          Exact extra subresource origin; never permits navigation away from the local base

      --heal
          On drift, hand only the broken edge to the model door (at most eight acts) and keep the repair only when the edge's original destination is observed. Needs a model source

      --fixture <FIXTURE>
          

      --manifest <MANIFEST>
          

      --route <ROUTE>
          

      --broker <BROKER>
          

      --gateway-keyring <GATEWAY_KEYRING>
          

      --gateway-key-id <GATEWAY_KEY_ID>
          

      --allow-act <ALLOW_ACT>
          Anchored action-name patterns a healing act may use for risky names (as in explore)

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm journey watch --help
Play a flow, draft or approved, from its entry to its last screen in a visible browser, paced for a person to follow (about 1.5 s per act), without a model. A look at what the flow does before approving it: never proof, never a capture, never an approval. A draft's act that looks destructive (delete, remove, drop, pay, purchase, transfer, send) is not performed, and the play stops there naming it, unless watch itself started the project's declared fixture (#515)

Usage: graphhelm journey watch [OPTIONS] <ID>

Arguments:
  <ID>
          The flow id (`<id>.journey.yaml`); a draft is accepted

Options:
      --path <PATH>
          The named path to play; defaults to `main`, else the first path

      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --project <PROJECT>
          

      --pace-ms <PACE_MS>
          Milliseconds to wait before each act (0 to 10000)
          
          [default: 1500]

      --allow-origin <ALLOW_ORIGIN>
          Exact extra subresource origin; never permits navigation away from the local base

      --window
          Play in a visible browser window on this machine. By default the browser is headless and the page streams as frames the Studio shows (`GET /v1/journeys/sessions/{id}/frame`)

  -h, --help
          Print help
