===== graphhelm keel --help
Build, verify, or query the Keel contract index, or check a diff against its card

Usage: graphhelm keel [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  test     Execute all journey flows in isolated validation mode and report browser coverage
  index    Scan tracked repository files into an index outside the repository
  verify   Refuse stale or changed index data
  verdict  Read verdict comments from an offline JSON snapshot, pinned to one head and reviewer
  query    Query declarations and paths from a verified index
  check    Compare a git diff with its Keel card: card bounds, scope (`keel.scope.path_outside_card`) and the surface the diff adds, under the shipped `keel.yaml`
  plan     Plan one task (#382 phase B): classify the paths it names under the shipped `keel.yaml` (invariant class, user-visible screen, code, docs), and print the `graphhelm-task-plan-v1` record: review count, proof type, skills, delegation and the shortest path to done. Deterministic. With `--events` (and `--execution`, `--keyring`, `--key-id`) it also records the plan as one `keel.plan` signal on that run, where the briefing reads it
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm keel check --help
Compare a git diff with its Keel card: card bounds, scope (`keel.scope.path_outside_card`) and the surface the diff adds, under the shipped `keel.yaml`

Usage: graphhelm keel check [OPTIONS] --diff <DIFF>

Options:
      --diff <DIFF>
          The git range to check, `<base>..<head>`

      --pretty
          

      --card <CARD>
          The card JSON (`keel-card.schema.json`). Without it the scope rule does not run

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --repo <REPO>
          The repository the range belongs to
          
          [default: .]

      --prove-new-tests
          Run each new Rust `#[test]` on the base (with the head's test grafted in) and on the head, in temporary worktrees; a test green on the base is `keel.test.green_on_parent`

      --prove-target-dir <PROVE_TARGET_DIR>
          Cargo target directory shared by every proving run. Default: `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`, else `graphhelm-keel-prove-target` under the system temporary directory

      --prove-timeout-secs <PROVE_TIMEOUT_SECS>
          Bound, in seconds, on one `cargo test` run (build included)
          
          [default: 900]

      --prove-command <PROVE_COMMAND>
          How to run one non-Rust new test and write a JUnit report to `{report}`, e.g. `npx vitest run {file} -t {name} --reporter=junit --outputFile={report}`. Only the report's testcase named exactly `{name}` decides. Without it those tests are unproven

      --events <EVENTS>
          With a card that names `journeys`: the run whose screen captures `keel check` reads (with `--execution`, `--keyring`, `--key-id`). Without them every touched screen is reported as having no capture read

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

      --route-proposal <ROUTE_PROPOSAL>
          Explicit graph-specific drafts to propose after a valid check; requires sealed records

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm mcp --help
Serves the chat surface: a stateless MCP server over stdio whose tools map 1:1 onto Public Runtime API requests. Speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 until stdin closes

Usage: graphhelm mcp [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --url <URL>
          The Public Runtime API's base URL for a direct or legacy port-discovery connection. Omit with `--discover` to resolve the active project's Runtime automatically. Loopback-only, fail-closed: userinfo is stripped before host inspection

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --token-file <TOKEN_FILE>
          File whose first line is the bearer token. Alternative: `GRAPHHELM_API_TOKEN`. The flag wins; both absent is a refusal naming the two options. The token value itself NEVER travels via argv

      --discover
          Discover the token and endpoint from a verified Runtime record. With `--url`, keeps the legacy behavior of following the Runtime on that port. Without `--url`, selects the active project's Runtime by identity, independent of its port. No live or unique identity match is a refusal; there is no fallback. `GRAPHHELM_API_TOKEN` is ignored in this mode

      --project <PROJECT>
          Project directory whose Runtime this MCP process is allowed to discover. With `--discover` and no `--url`, defaults to the process working directory

      --actor <ACTOR>
          The actor every mutation is attributed to (the serve layer's actor id rules). OPTIONAL because one `.mcp.json` is shared by every session in a repository, so a literal here makes every session the same actor (#1058). A non-empty `GRAPHHELM_ACTOR` wins over this flag (#389), so a lane can sign as itself under the shared registration; absent from both doors is a refusal, never a default

      --actor-type <ACTOR_TYPE>
          `agent` (the chat is an agent) or `owner` for an owner-driven chat
          
          [default: agent]

      --model <MODEL>
          The model this session is running, verbatim and opaque (`claude-opus-5`, `gpt-6-astra`). ABSENT IS ABSENT: no default, and the Runtime never infers one from the route -- a `claude_subscription` route lets the CLI choose its own model, so a route-derived guess would be a label the run cannot support (#1054)

      --effort <EFFORT>
          `low`, `medium` or `high`. A CLOSED vocabulary, so a wrong value is refusable here rather than rendered as a badge nobody can interpret

      --capability-token-file <CAPABILITY_TOKEN_FILE>
          File holding one per-contribution MCP capability token (#213), JSON, matching `graphhelm_tool_broker::mcp_capability::McpCapabilityToken`'s wire shape. Opt-in by PRESENCE, not by `--actor-type`: `--actor-type agent` is the default for ordinary chat sessions with no contribution to scope, so requiring this flag there would refuse the common case, not the threat. The party that decides whether an extension contribution's session gets this flag is whatever harness launches `graphhelm mcp` on the contribution's behalf -- never the contribution's own declared config, since that would let a hostile contribution simply omit the flag and keep today's unrestricted access. When present, requires `--package` (the digest every presented tool call is checked fresh against); when absent, every tool is reachable exactly as before #213

      --package <PACKAGE>
          The extension package this session's capability token was minted against (required alongside `--capability-token-file`). Its digest is recomputed fresh on every tool call, never cached for the session's lifetime -- a package edited mid-session immediately stales any token minted before the edit (#213 blueprint T2)

      --capability-audit-log <CAPABILITY_AUDIT_LOG>
          Append-only JSONL audit trail (required alongside `--capability-token-file`): one redacted `McpCapabilityAuditRecord` per tool call, allowed or refused. Never call arguments, never the token's own bytes. Read with `jq` or any line-oriented JSON tool; a dedicated reader/summarizer command is a named follow-up, not built by #213

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm quality --help
Quality-gate operations: the thymus ritual and the certification stamp

Usage: graphhelm quality [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:

  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

===== graphhelm quality certify --help
Runs a registered gate against the pathogen suite; on FULL rejection, stamps GateCertified onto the stream (what the certified-or-not-at-all precondition reads)

Usage: graphhelm quality certify [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS> --gate <GATE>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --gate <GATE>
          The registered gate id. The registry is closed; an unrecognised id is refused and the refusal names what IS registered.
          
          Deliberately does NOT enumerate the gates. clap renders this from a compile-time literal, so it cannot be derived from the registry and could only be kept in sync by memory -- in a different file from the check that decides membership, and read by the operator BEFORE anything runs. The refusal message is the single place that enumerates.

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm serve --help
Usage: graphhelm serve [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS> --bind <BIND>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          The events directory the server reads and writes through the shared command layer; the same directory a co-located `graphhelm execution`/`events` invocation would use. Created if it does not already exist

      --pretty
          

      --bind <BIND>
          The address to bind, e.g. `127.0.0.1:8080` or `127.0.0.1:0` for an OS-assigned port. Refused unless it names a loopback address — the Public Runtime API is never exposed beyond localhost

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --manifest <MANIFEST>
          The MODEL half of the real-executor wiring: `--manifest`, `--broker` and `--route` are all-or-none (#1066). With them, cognitive nodes (agent, planner, classifier, evaluator) run on the named route. Without them, cognitive nodes are answered by node fixtures. Any real half also requires `--keyring`/`--key-id`. Absent entirely, together with the tool half below, `serve` stays the fixture-only 05a server

      --gateway-manifest <GATEWAY_MANIFEST>
          A route manifest the Studio's Models panel lists and writes (`GET`/`PUT /v1/gateway/routes`) WITHOUT wiring any executor: cognitive nodes stay on node fixtures (#585: the journey fixture shows the Add model form this way). `--manifest` names the manifest itself, so the two are refused together

      --broker <BROKER>
          The credential broker directory the model half leases from. See `--manifest`

      --keyring <KEYRING>
          The sealed keyring evidence is sealed under; with `--key-id` it is its own all-or-none pair, usable alone (sealing-only, for `signal`) and REQUIRED with either real half

      --key-id <KEY_ID>
          

      --events-key-file <EVENTS_KEY_FILE>
          Read the sealing key once at start from this owner-only file (64 lowercase hex characters) instead of `GRAPHHELM_EVENTS_KEY`. Needs `--keyring`; refused together with the variable. The key stays in this process and is never passed to a child

      --route <ROUTE>
          The manifest route cognitive nodes run on by default (a request may name another). See `--manifest`

      --staging <STAGING>
          The TOOL half of the real-executor wiring: `--staging` and `--allow-program` are all-or-none (#1066), and need NO model credential. With them, tool nodes run on the real tool host: one Tier 1 worktree per execution under this staging directory, kept across that execution's tool calls and removed when its drive ends; a `commit` node lands `refs/graphhelm/executions/<execution id>` in the project — a plain ref, never a branch, never the operator's checkout. Without them, tool nodes are answered by node fixtures

      --project <PROJECT>
          The deployer's own default workspace root for `start`/`resume`, used whenever a request omits `"project"` — never required, never part of the real-executor group above. Absent, the prior behavior is unchanged: the server's own process working directory. Exists because neither `start` nor `resume`'s MCP tool schema exposes a `project` field (issue #82) — an operator confined to the MCP surface has no channel to avoid the default colliding with `--staging` when the server happens to run from a `--staging` ancestor, so the deployer must be able to fix the default once, the same way `--staging` itself is fixed once, rather than every caller needing infrastructure knowledge it was never given. Meaningful only alongside the tool half (`--staging`/`--allow-program`; `drive` only ever consults it there); given without it, it is accepted but silently unused

      --workspace-root <WORKSPACE_ROOT>
          The agent workspace root (#360) that `GET /v1/workspaces` lists and the owner's `POST /v1/workspaces/sweep` sweeps. Nothing in a request names a path; without this flag both routes refuse naming it

      --workspace-sweep-seconds <WORKSPACE_SWEEP_SECONDS>
          Sweep eligible workspaces every N seconds with --workspace-root (0 disables; otherwise 60..=86400). Uses the same rules as workspace sweep --apply
          
          [default: 1800]

      --slot-root <SLOT_ROOTS>
          A build-slot root (#612) whose queue `GET /v1/workspaces/slots` reports; repeatable (for example `D:/gh` and `D:/gh/b`). Read-only: the Runtime never queues, cancels or reorders

      --handover-install <HANDOVER_INSTALL>
          The install root `graphhelm update` writes (`<root>/bin/graphhelm` and its `<root>/.graphhelm-installed-head` stamp; #1523, D-059). When the stamp changes, this Runtime starts that binary with its own arguments and inherited environment, and hands it the port and the events lock once it reports ready; a binary that fails to start leaves this Runtime serving

      --supervise
          Stay as a small hidden parent that runs the Runtime as its child with these same arguments and environment (the keys stay in memory) and starts it again, with backoff, when it exits unexpectedly. A clean stop does not restart; after a handover the parent watches the successor. Stopping this parent stops its Runtime (#1962)

      --sweep-interval <SWEEP_INTERVAL>
          Run the customs sweep automatically every N seconds, journalling each one as `SweepCaller::Tick`.
          
          OFF UNLESS ASKED FOR, and that default is a safety property rather than caution. A tick is a BACKGROUND WRITER: it appends to the same streams operators are mutating, so with it on by default every existing caller that compares two head sequences across a request pair would start seeing a third append it never made. `--sweep-interval` makes the writer a deployment decision, and makes the tick testable without arming it for everyone.

      --read-audit <READ_AUDIT>
          Append every request and the exact bytes served to this file, as JSON lines.
          
          Off unless asked for: the recorded bodies carry the operator's own execution data, so recording is a deliberate act rather than a default. The file is written OUTSIDE the event store on purpose - a surface that wrote into the execution stream in order to observe it would advance `headSequence` without advancing `lastEventAt`, and head movement would stop implying progress.

      --require-lane-credential
          #1148: refuse a `task.*` record authenticated by the shared agent session token, so only a lane's own credential (`graphhelm tasks credential`) can sign one. Off by default: the owner flips it after minting one credential per lane, so no record is lost in between

      --confine-paths
          #1328: refuse any host path a request names (`file`, `fixtures`, `manifest`, `evidenceOut`, `project`, and synthesize's and probe's paths) that resolves outside the allowed roots (`--project` and every `--path-root`). Off by default: lanes post paths from worktrees outside the project, so the owner turns it on with their roots after a restart, the same way `--require-lane-credential` is flipped

      --path-root <PATH_ROOTS>
          #1328: a directory a request path may also resolve under while `--confine-paths` is on, beside `--project`; repeatable (for example `D:/gh` and `D:/gh/b`)

      --tests-runner <TESTS_RUNNER>
          The bare program name a `tests` tool node runs, resolved on the child's PATH (see `--path-prepend`). Host configuration, never caller input
          
          [default: cargo]

      --allow-program <ALLOW_PROGRAM>
          Repeatable; the other half of the `--staging` pair (#583, #1066). There is no default: the set of programs an execution may spawn is declared per run, so the journal records a choice rather than an inheritance. The tests runner is host configuration (`--tests-runner`) and is not listed here

      --path-prepend <PATH_PREPEND>
          Repeatable; directories joined ahead of the child's inherited PATH

  -h, --help
          Print help (see a summary with '-h')

===== graphhelm setup --help
Read-only inventory and preview for adopting GraphHelm methodology into supported hosts

Usage: graphhelm setup [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> --home <HOME>

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --project <PROJECT>
          

      --home <HOME>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --dry-run
          

      --resolve <RESOLVE>
          Owner decision for one unresolved item: `<item>=keep`, `<item>=replace:<file>` whose bytes are the reviewed replacement, or `<item>=graphhelm-block` (the marked GraphHelm + Keel block, upserted into the item's current bytes). `home/.claude.json=register-mcp` or `project/.mcp.json=register-mcp` opts in to the `graphhelm` MCP registration. Repeatable. With any `--resolve`, `--out` is required because the resulting plan carries bytes that never go to stdout

      --out <OUT>
          Write the plan (preview, or the applyable plan built from `--resolve`) to this private, owner-only file. Its exact digest is what `--accept` takes

      --state-root <STATE_ROOT>
          Private recovery storage, outside the project and host roots

      --apply <APPLY>
          Apply this private, reviewed plan after checking its exact digest

      --plan <PLAN>
          Preview this exact reviewed plan (redacted: digest, scopes, decisions, operation paths, digests and byte lengths; never the `after` text), or bind it to a verification attempt

      --verify <VERIFY>
          Validate an activation receipt against --plan and current installed bytes. No trusted host observer is shipped; user-authored JSON remains observer_missing

      --accept <ACCEPT>
          

      --package <PACKAGES>
          Explicit local package trees; both must match the reviewed Extension pins

      --recover <RECOVER>
          Reconcile an interrupted transaction using its private journal

      --install-observer <INSTALL_OBSERVERS>
          Install a browser journey observer in `--project` by running the install commands the preview lists under `observers` (npm and npx, network). `playwright` is the default observer; `e2e` is opt-in and needs a model key for agent steps. Repeatable
          
          [possible values: playwright, e2e]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm tool invoke --help
One authorized tool call, end to end: authorize -> route by tier -> execute -> record

Usage: graphhelm tool invoke [OPTIONS] --project <PROJECT> --staging <STAGING> --request <REQUEST> --actor <ACTOR>

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --project <PROJECT>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --staging <STAGING>
          

      --protected <PROTECTED>
          Repeatable; directories the workspace must never overlap (keyring, broker, events)

      --request <REQUEST>
          The ToolCall as JSON (checked deserialization: unknown fields refused)

      --actor <ACTOR>
          

      --capability <CAPABILITIES>
          Repeatable; builds the lease: repository.read, repository.write, shell.execute, tests.execute

      --allow-program <ALLOW_PROGRAMS>
          Repeatable; the lease's shell program allowlist (bare names)

      --tests-runner <TESTS_RUNNER>
          [default: cargo]

      --capture-out <CAPTURE_OUT>
          REQUIRED on every invoke (checked as GHCLI012, not by the parser, so the refusal speaks the envelope): captured stream bytes are written here as files

      --keep-workspace
          Debug only: skip workspace cleanup and report what was kept

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm update --help
Update GraphHelm itself: fast-forward the clone this binary comes from to `origin/main` (only a clean `main`), then reinstall the CLI from it with `cargo install`

Usage: graphhelm update [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --source <SOURCE>
          The GraphHelm clone. Defaults to `GRAPHHELM_SOURCE`, then to GraphHelm's own install clone `~/.graphhelm/source` (#1134), created from the origin of the clone this binary was built from

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --keep-local
          Build the clone even when it could not be brought up to origin/main (local changes, another branch, a diverged main). Without it such an update stops before compiling

      --check
          Build nothing: fetch origin/main and exit non-zero when this binary was not built from it (#1244), so a check never runs on a CLI older than main

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm wake-wait --help
The wake doorbell's sidecar: creates the rendezvous for an opaque id, blocks for free, exits 0 on ring / 3 on timeout / 2 on unusable arguments. Content never crosses: the woken host learns only THAT it should re-read its log

Usage: graphhelm wake-wait [OPTIONS] --events <EVENTS> --session-id <SESSION_ID>

Options:
      --events <EVENTS>
          The events directory holding the lease this session armed

      --pretty
          

      --execution <EXECUTION>
          The execution whose stream carries the lease. Optional when the directory holds one

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --session-id <SESSION_ID>
          The session whose OWN lease this waits on. The rendezvous and the deadline both come from that lease — this surface used to take a rendezvous id and a timeout from the caller, which made two numbers answer "how long before I give up" with nothing tying them together

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm workspace --help
Agent workspaces (#360): `claim` a worktree with its own cargo target, temp and log directories under one root, `release` it when the task is done, `list` them, and `sweep` (the owner's) removes released workspaces that are still clean at the released commit

Usage: graphhelm workspace [OPTIONS] <COMMAND>

Commands:
  claim    Create `<root>/<lane>/<task>/` with a git worktree (`wt`) and `target`, `tmp` and `logs` directories, record the claim, and print the environment to use
  release  Declare the task done: records the worktree's HEAD. Deletes nothing
  list     Every recorded workspace with its state, size and live git facts. Read-only
  sweep    Remove released workspaces that are clean and still at the released commit, ignored files included. A dry run unless `--apply`. Never touches a path the ledger did not create, never follows a link, and keeps any workspace whose worktree contains one
  remove   Remove one worktree or directory without ever following a link (#1663). A linked git worktree is stopped, unlinked, its uncommitted work saved, unregistered and deleted; any other directory has its links unlinked and is deleted. Use it instead of `rm -rf` or `git worktree remove --force`, which follow junctions. Exit 3 when it could not finish
  slot     Run one command under the root's build slot: one at a time, in arrival order, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and the current worktree's own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<cwd>/target`. A waiter that dies loses its place by itself (its ticket's OS lock is released). The command's exit code is ours
  help     Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm workspace claim --help
Create `<root>/<lane>/<task>/` with a git worktree (`wt`) and `target`, `tmp` and `logs` directories, record the claim, and print the environment to use

Usage: graphhelm workspace claim [OPTIONS] --root <ROOT> --lane <LANE> --task <TASK> --repo <REPO>

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --root <ROOT>
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --lane <LANE>
          

      --task <TASK>
          

      --repo <REPO>
          The git repository the worktree is added to

      --base <BASE>
          The commit-ish the new branch starts from. Defaults to `origin/main`

      --branch <BRANCH>
          The branch to create. Defaults to `issue-<task>-<lane>`

  -h, --help
          Print help

Usage: graphhelm workspace help slot [COMMAND]

Commands:
  status  Who holds the build slot (lane, label, for how long) and who waits, in order, with their wait. Read-only apart from removing a dead waiter's ticket

===== graphhelm workspace remove --help
Remove one worktree or directory without ever following a link (#1663). A linked git worktree is stopped, unlinked, its uncommitted work saved, unregistered and deleted; any other directory has its links unlinked and is deleted. Use it instead of `rm -rf` or `git worktree remove --force`, which follow junctions. Exit 3 when it could not finish

Usage: graphhelm workspace remove [OPTIONS] <PATH>

Arguments:
  <PATH>
          The worktree or directory to delete

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --repo <REPO>
          A repository whose registered worktrees a plain directory must not contain

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --leftovers <LEFTOVERS>
          A worktree's uncommitted work is saved under `<leftovers>/<directory name>/` first
          
          [default: D:/_merge-leftovers]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm workspace slot --help
Run one command under the root's build slot: one at a time, in arrival order, with `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS` and the current worktree's own `CARGO_TARGET_DIR=<cwd>/target`. A waiter that dies loses its place by itself (its ticket's OS lock is released). The command's exit code is ours

Usage: graphhelm workspace slot [OPTIONS] --root <ROOT> --lane <LANE> -- <COMMAND>...
       graphhelm workspace slot <COMMAND>

Commands:
  status  Who holds the build slot (lane, label, for how long) and who waits, in order, with their wait. Read-only apart from removing a dead waiter's ticket
  help    Print this message or the help of the given subcommand(s)

Arguments:
  <COMMAND>...
          The command and its arguments, after `--`

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --root <ROOT>
          

      --lane <LANE>
          

      --label <LABEL>
          What this build is for, shown to the other waiters (e.g. `pr405-review`)
          
          [default: build]

      --jobs <JOBS>
          [default: 12]

      --clean-workspace
          Before the command, `cargo clean -p` every package of the current cargo workspace out of the target in use. Third-party crates stay. Refuses if the clean cannot run or fails

      --shared-target
          Build in `<root>/target-shared` instead of the worktree's own target. UNSAFE for tests: cargo treats another worktree's path-dependency artifacts as fresh, so a run can test bytes it did not build (#361). Opt-in only, for builds whose result does not vouch for a tree

      --max-wait <MAX_WAIT>
          Give up after this many minutes of waiting (fractions allowed). Without it a waiter waits as long as it takes (#540). A waiter that gives up keeps its place for 30 minutes: the same lane and label queueing again within that time are served where they first arrived

      --priority
          Go next after the current holder, ahead of every other waiter; never preempts the holder. Only for a lane listed in `<root>/.graphhelm-workspaces/slot-priority-lanes` (one lane per line, written by the owner); any other lane is refused and its command never runs (#540)

      --stage <STAGE>
          What this build is for (#1470). A waiting `review` or `merge` job is admitted before every waiting `implement` job, whatever the arrival order; it never preempts the holder, and an owner `--priority` waiter still goes first
          
          [default: implement]
          [possible values: implement, review, merge]

  -h, --help
          Print help

===== graphhelm workspace sweep --help
Remove released workspaces that are clean and still at the released commit, ignored files included. A dry run unless `--apply`. Never touches a path the ledger did not create, never follows a link, and keeps any workspace whose worktree contains one

Usage: graphhelm workspace sweep [OPTIONS]

Options:
      --pretty
          

      --root <ROOT>
          The claim ledger root swept for released workspaces. Not used with `--merged-branch`

      --apply
          Remove what the dry run lists. Without it nothing is changed

      --json
          Print the JSON envelope even at a terminal (#1172). Without it a terminal gets the rendered summary, and everything that is not a terminal gets the envelope either way

      --merged-branch <MERGED_BRANCH>
          Merge cleanup (#1456): remove every worktree of this merged branch, the review checkouts detached at `--head`, the `--target` directories and the local branch, in one call

      --all
          Machine cleanup (#1578): every registered worktree of `--repo` and every build cache under the slot and target roots that is merged/closed (or clean, pushed and idle) and not held by a live process; then `git worktree prune`. Locked worktrees are skipped and reported

      --sweep-root <SWEEP_ROOTS>
          A root whose build caches `--all` sweeps (repeatable). Defaults to the machine's slot and target roots (D:/gh, D:/gh/b, D:/gh/c, D:/gh/sub, D:/ghb, D:/ghc, D:/ghopt, C:/ghc, C:/gh, C:/w/a, C:/w/b, C:/w/c, C:/w/d)

      --pr-states <PR_STATES>
          A JSON file `{"<branch>": "MERGED" | "CLOSED" | "OPEN"}` for `--all`. Without it the states are read once with `gh pr list --state all`; content already in origin/main counts as merged either way

      --idle-hours <IDLE_HOURS>
          `--all`: a pushed, unmerged worktree or a build cache untouched this many hours is idle
          
          [default: 24]

      --repo <REPO>
          The repository whose worktrees are listed (any of its worktrees, or the main checkout). With `--all` it defaults to the current directory

      --pr <PR>
          The merged PR number; names the leftovers folder. Defaults to the branch name

      --head <HEAD>
          The reviewed head sha: detached review checkouts at it are removed too

      --target <TARGETS>
          A per-PR build directory to delete (repeatable). Links are removed, never followed

      --keep-worktree <KEEP_WORKTREES>
          A lane's single reused review worktree (repeatable): kept, and its checkout of the PR is moved off to `--base` instead of being removed. Its shared target is never named here

      --base <BASE>
          Where a kept worktree is detached to
          
          [default: origin/main]

      --leftovers <LEFTOVERS>
          Uncommitted work found in a worktree is saved under `<leftovers>/<PR>/` before removal
          
          [default: D:/_merge-leftovers]

  -h, --help
          Print help
